posts.title: Are You Actually Using the Model You Selected?
posts.author: Lucas L.
posts.excerpt: A model picker or an API response that repeats the model name is not proof of which model handled the request. For hosted models you cannot hash production weights, so the practical approach is a transaction evidence chain that records what you requested, what the service says it selected, which provider handled it, and what you were charged.

posts.title: Speak LLM: A Practical Glossary for Better Agent Outcomes
posts.author: Lucas L.
posts.excerpt: A practical glossary of agent and LLM workflow phrases such as smoke test, blast radius, regression, harness, and negative path. The post explains why precise vocabulary improves outcomes, and gives ready-to-paste prompts for investigation, planning, implementation, and verification.

posts.title: Prompt Smarter: Leveraging LLM Insights for Enhanced Outcomes
posts.author: Lucas L.
posts.excerpt: A practical explanation of how LLMs process prompts through tokenisation, embeddings, attention, prediction, and sampling. The post connects those mechanics to prompt structure, reasoning effort, temperature, security analysis prompts, coding prompts, and the larger shift from text generation to agent harnesses where provider choice becomes an architecture decision.

posts.title: Token Use Optimizations: How to keep agent sessions fast, cheap, and useful
posts.author: Lucas L.
posts.excerpt: Agentic tool sessions like Claude Code become expensive and less reliable when conversation history, file reads, shell output, CLAUDE.md, skills and responses accumulate. This post provides token optimisation tips for agentic CLI work. It shows how to measure context, clear between unrelated tasks, compact before the window is forced to compact, keep CLAUDE.md as an index, constrain shell and MCP output, delegate noisy work to subagents, and move repeatable workflows into skills and hooks.

posts.title: Token Economics: Best practices for managing context windows
posts.author: Lucas L.
posts.excerpt: Claude Code as well as other agentic CLI tools re-evaluate the full context window on every turn, including conversation history, CLAUDE.md, memory, skills, and tool context. Token costs compound across a session because each message carries the accumulated weight of everything before it. This post consolidates techniques for managing context window pressure, reducing token waste, and maintaining model performance in agentic CLI workflows.

posts.title: Agent Harnesses, Skills, and Tool Runtimes: The Architecture of Frontier Models
posts.author: Lucas L.
posts.excerpt: The modern frontier model is no longer a standalone chatbot. In practical deployments, the model is only one layer in a much larger system made up of orchestration logic, tool discovery, execution runtimes, security boundaries, memory handling, and approval controls. This post examines what agent harnesses actually are, how skills, MCP servers, and tool runtimes fit into the architecture, and how OpenAI, Google, and Anthropic differ in their approach to building systems around frontier models.

posts.title: Zero-Day Discovery at Machine Speed and the Defensive Shift Ahead
posts.author: Lucas L.
posts.excerpt: Anthropic reports frontier LLMs have achieved autonomous zero day discovery and exploitation, identifying twenty-year-old heap overflows in the Linux kernel and executing unauthenticated credential theft against Ghost CMS. These agents eliminate the human bottleneck by performing the entire research lifecycle at machine speed. As the capability curve for offensive AI scales exponentially, defenders must adopt agentic security workflows and memory safe architectures to secure an increasingly transparent attack surface.

posts.title: Detecting AI Prompt Injection in the Wild
posts.author: Lucas L.
posts.excerpt: Building EKFiddle rules and other queries to detect indirect prompt injection, AI ClickFix, CSS hidden text traps, and credential exfiltration targeting autonomous AI agents.
